info.name: TetraFi API
info.description: Generated from the TetraFi integrator specification. Set baseUrl, apiKey and signingSecret in your local collection variables. Start with GET /api/v1/assets. Replace angle-bracket placeholders with real values before sending other requests; review each write rather than running the entire collection. Never share populated credentials.

exec: // Never retain headers from an earlier signed send when signing is turned off.
// Resolve variables ONCE, including dynamic variables, before hashing and sending.
if (!parts) throw new Error('Set baseUrl to an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL');
// Encode explicitly and disable subsequent transport encoding, so the signed
// target is exactly what is sent. Keep already percent-encoded bytes unchanged.
if (pm.request.body.mode !== 'raw') throw new Error('Signing supports raw request bodies only');
// JSON comments are not valid API input and Postman would strip them AFTER
// signing. Refuse them rather than signing bytes different from the wire.
if (!/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i.test(secret)) throw new Error('signingSecret must contain 64 hexadecimal characters');
// A write needs a nonce accepted once per key: a new random UUID on every send.
if (nonce !== null && !/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}$/.test(nonce)) throw new Error('Could not generate an X-Nonce');
const canonical = [timestamp, ...(nonce === null ? [] : [nonce]), method, pathWithQuery, digest].join('\n');
if (nonce !== null) pm.request.headers.upsert({ key: 'X-Nonce', value: nonce });

List tradable assets

The Assets, variants and deployments the workspace can trade.

request.description:
Read up to 20 resources in one request

Each item is a GET of an operation in this reference that answers JSON, written as its path and query. Every item runs exactly as a separate GET by the same caller: the same permissions, scopes, workspace checks, response body and error body. The batch authenticates once and counts as one request per item against the caller's rate limit, all taken before any item runs (429 `RATE_LIMITED` refuses the whole batch). Items are independent and not atomic: once admitted the batch answers 200, and each item carries its own `status`, `etag` and `body`, in request order. Item bodies are limited to 8 MiB in all (an item past it answers 413 `BATCH_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE`), and a batch with its related reads makes at most 200 reads (past it an item answers 429 `SUB_REQUEST_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`). The answer is `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. A malformed batch, more than 20 items, a non-GET item, a url that is not a GET operation of this reference, or a stream, export or file read is refused as a whole before any item runs, with `details.itemId` naming the item. A signed API-key request cannot be batched: send its reads separately. An API key or OAuth client batches only operations of this reference; each item must be dispatched to the operation it names, else it answers `BATCH_UNKNOWN_ROUTE`. An item keeps its `Deprecation`, `Sunset`, `Link`, `Retry-After` and `Cache-Control` headers in `headers`.
Get the current credential

Exchange client credentials for a token

RFC 6749 client-credentials grant for active service accounts. Supply grant_type=client_credentials, client_id=<service-account UUID>, and client_secret=<full tfk_live_... or tfk_test_... service-account API key>. Client credentials may instead be sent with HTTP Basic authentication. Tokens use the configured auth.jwtExpirySeconds capped at 900 seconds and carry the service account's current workspace role, effective permissions, and effective API scopes.

List orders

Lists Basic orders using the same envelope as GET /orders/{orderId}. Required API-key scope: `orders_read`; a member session needs permission to view or place orders. Newest first by created time and id. A status filter is applied to stored order facts first and then to each order's canonical public status; a filtered page keeps reading until it holds limit items or the orders end, within a bounded scan. A page shorter than limit carries a nextCursor only when that scan reached its limit, and then says so with scanLimitReached: follow nextCursor until null. A cursor is bound to the caller, workspace and exact filters; a malformed, foreign or deleted anchor is INVALID_CURSOR.

header.description: Makes a retry safe. Required for API keys (a missing key answers 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED); optional for signed-in members. 1 to 255 bytes, unique per order you mean to place; a UUID is a good choice. A retry with the same key and the same body, from the same credential's owner in the same workspace within 24 hours, returns the first answer and never places a second order. The same key with a different body answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; another principal's key answers 403 IDEMPOTENCY_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED. A retry that arrives while the first request is still running waits for it, and answers 409 ORDER_IN_PROGRESS (with Retry-After) if it is still running after 30 seconds. Refusals are not stored: after one, fix the request and send it again with the same key or a new one.

request.description:
Place an order

Place an order by the id of a quote you hold (`{quoteId}` from POST /quotes). A Basic venue quote becomes a venue trade (`basicTrade`). Each quote is ordered once: the same quote again answers QUOTE_ALREADY_ORDERED, and a replay with the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the first answer. Read what a quote produced with GET /orders/by-quote/{quoteId}.

Get an order

Returns the latest stored order after a provider refresh. For REST polling, wait 10–15 seconds between reads and honor `Retry-After` on 429; do not poll in a tight loop. After a webhook delivery, perform this GET to obtain the complete current projection. Never put an API key in a URL. Terminality is order-kind dependent: route and atomic venue orders normally complete at `settled`, while claim-based or deferred products may advance to `finalized`.

header.description: Required for API keys. Cancellation is naturally idempotent by order id.

request.description:
Cancel an order

Cancels an undispatched Basic order or a pay-in still awaiting funds. Returns the same order envelope as GET, with status cancelled and terminal true. Repeating cancellation leaves the order unchanged. A durable dispatch claim, a progressed funding leg, or a terminal outcome refuses with ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE and details.status. Required API-key scope: `orders_write`, with an Idempotency-Key; a member session needs permission to place orders. No venue cancellation is attempted.

Recover the order produced by a held quote

Read-only recovery, independent of quote-stream completion and quote expiry. Required API-key scope: `orders_read`; the caller must be allowed to view orders in the selected workspace. ordered names the Basic venue trade address; read that resource for current state. notOrdered is returned only after native order and consumption reads succeed. An unresolved claim returns unknown, never permission to submit again. Foreign and unknown quote ids share 404.

Get indicative prices

Indicative per-venue prices for one pair, from the latest observed prices; no venue is called.

request.description:
Request quotes

Ask every eligible venue for prices on one asset pair. `kind` selects the request body: `pair` for a new request, or `requote` to ask an earlier quote's venue again (the new quote names it in `requoteOf`; the earlier quote stays held until it expires, and a requote more than 10 minutes after that expiry is 410 REQUOTE_WINDOW_CLOSED). A missing `kind` is 400 QUOTE_REQUEST_KIND_REQUIRED and an unknown one 400 QUOTE_REQUEST_KIND_INVALID. The answer is a PairQuoteSet: its quotes are held for you, and GET /quotes/requests/{quoteRequestId} reads it again. A request that asks a venue is limited to one every 3 seconds per caller (429 QUOTE_RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After). `firmness` is `indicative`, `firm` or `auto` (the default): indicative never asks a desk for a firm price, firm asks every eligible desk, and auto asks a production desk only when you name it in filters.venues.include or requote its card. Required API-key scope: `quotes_request`, on a key that also holds `orders_write`. A firm venue-account quote also needs `workspace_venue_trade`, the venue's switch on for the key and request signing; without them the card is indicative, with sourceRefusal venueTradeScopeRequired. A key has no default wallet: name a trading wallet per chain in source.tradingWallets (CAIP-2 chain to financial-account id), either a workspace custody wallet or an organisation wallet granted to the key; a personal wallet is 409 PERSONAL_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED. deliverTo is for member sessions only: a key's requote naming one is 409 REQUOTE_REFUSED (details.reason deliverToNotPermitted). Every refusal uses the ApiError body.

Read a quote request's recorded answer

The quotes, sources and orders of one asset-pair POST /quotes answer. Required API-key scope: `quotes_read`. Immediate reads use the same held request handed to the asynchronous evidence writer; later reads recover its durable record. Readable by the principal that asked, by a member session allowed to view the workspace's orders, and by an API key with the additional orders_read scope when an order was placed on one of its quotes in that workspace. Unknown and foreign ids are the same 404. A request lost in a crash before persistence returns 404 QUOTE_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND; its unpersisted quotes are also lost, so request fresh quotes. Genuine store or read failures return retryable 503 QUOTE_REQUEST_UNAVAILABLE with details.retryAfter and Retry-After. requestedByYou says whether the caller asked; only then can it order these quotes.

Read balances across workspace accounts

Cache-only balance observations across readable workspace wallets and venue accounts. Each wallet accountId is its walletId; venue accounts retain their native venueAccountId. amount is total holdings in exact decimal asset units, asOf is the source observation time, and freshness distinguishes stale or partial observations. No provider request or refresh is started. Accounts without a readable observation are named in unavailable with a cause code, never a fabricated zero. Bank balances are unobservable. Personal wallets are excluded. The wallet resource policy must allow read_balances; a venue account needs the caller to be allowed to view wallets, in a company or broker workspace or as an admitted LP taker, exactly as its own balance read. Required API-key scope: `treasury_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. Hidden accounts affect neither rows nor cursors. unavailable is repeated on each filtered page. Cursors bind to the workspace, caller, filters and ordered visible row identities; restart if those identities change.

Read the workspace's verification state and the capabilities it allows

The workspace's KYB state (`workspace.kybStatus`) and, for each capability, whether it is
allowed now or blocked, with each blocker's code and the step that clears it. The quote and
order routes enforce the same decision. An API key needs the `compliance_read` scope and reads
only the workspace it is bound to.

Read the workspace's effective fee schedule

Current and upcoming effective fees for this workspace, readable by any current member. Required API-key scope: `fee_schedule_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. Rates are decimal strings in parts per million. A schedule that cannot be read answers 503 FEE_SCHEDULE_UNAVAILABLE, never a partial or zero schedule.

Read the cross-venue settlement plan

A read-only snapshot of what is due across the workspace's venue accounts. Unknown deadlines remain unknown. Per-source read failures are explicit and make the plan incomplete. Reading creates no transfer, reservation, approval request or LP instruction. Required API-key scope: `settlements_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. The key's owner must also be allowed to view the workspace's settlements.

List trades

The one trade history. Projections: scope=workspace (default) reads the workspace's taker orders and venue trades; a caller not allowed to view the workspace's compliance records reads only their own, whatever the scope. scope=mine reads the caller's own (a member session only). scope=umbrella reads a broker's clients' orders with each client category's field visibility (a member session allowed to view client compliance records). perspective=maker reads an LP workspace's fills with pseudonymised counterparties (a member session allowed to view settlements); with settlementStage or minAgeSeconds, its unsettled orders by stage (a member session allowed to view bilateral documents). The default perspective is taker in every workspace. Every row carries tradeId, kind (order or venueTrade) and projection. Page with limit and cursor; format=csv returns the same filtered rows. Required API-key scope: `trades_read`; CSV is a member session only.

Get a trade

One trade through the same projection as the list: the workspace's or the caller's own taker order or venue trade, a broker umbrella record with the client category's field visibility, or an LP's fill with pseudonymised counterparties. Taker orders keep their detail fields at the top level. Accepts a member session or an API key with trades_read.

taker (default) or maker, as on the list
Maker: the LP's own venue that filled it
Maker: protocol, venueAccount or all

request.description:
Get trade settlement

One trade's settlement state. The taker perspective is the order's settlement detail (required API-key scope: `settlements_read`; the caller must be allowed to view settlements). The maker perspective is the LP's settlement pipeline for the order, a member-session read for a member allowed to view bilateral documents. Each perspective answers exactly what its own route answers.

perspective=maker: the LP's own venue; omitted reads every owned venue

List a trade's settlement obligations

request.description:
Read the venue account's balances at its venue

The caller must be allowed to view wallets in a company or broker workspace (or be an admitted LP taker). API keys and OAuth clients additionally require treasury_read; this read never authorizes a payment. Read through the connection holding the account's balance credential, a configured one first (its `connectionId` and execution type are in the body); the observation, staleness and display-value rules are those of the venue-connection balance read, so a balance key held only by a disabled venue returns its last-known balance. 409 VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDS_IN_WALLETS for an account whose money is in the company's own wallets, VENUE_ACCOUNT_REVERIFY_REQUIRED when no current key holds its balance, VENUE_ACCOUNT_REVOKED for a disconnected account, VENUE_ACCOUNT_VENUE_UNKNOWN when its venue is not recognised; 404 VENUE_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED whenever the caller's read authority has ended, whether the check before the read or a recheck during it sees it (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its owner lost permission to view wallets, its membership or taker admission); a session that has itself ended answers 401.

Read one venue account's credit

The account's credit as the Treasury credit card shows it: the provider's reported line (limit, used, available, overrun), the agreed facility, open credit commitments and the signed positions, each with its own observation time. The caller must be allowed to view the workspace's wallets and credit; an API key or OAuth client additionally needs treasury_read. Figures come from the account's last recorded ledger observation; this read makes no provider call (read the account ledger for a live read). A component that could not be read is `unavailable` with its code, never zero. 403 INSUFFICIENT_WORKSPACE_PERMISSION without permission to view credit; 404 VENUE_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND, also for another workspace's account; 409 VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDS_IN_WALLETS for a wallet-based venue; 503 VENUE_ACCOUNT_ELIGIBILITY_UNAVAILABLE when account access cannot be read.

Read the venue account's deposit history

The caller must be allowed to view wallets in a company or broker workspace (or be an admitted LP taker). API keys and OAuth clients additionally require treasury_read. Read through the configured connection holding the account's balance credential, with the venue-connection deposit-history rules. Each first answer reads the venue's credit history for `lookbackDays` (1 to 30, default 7), ending now. Optional `limit` (1 to 200) and `cursor` page credits oldest first by observation time and venue deposit id. Follow `nextCursor` until null. A cursor freezes the window and binds its workspace, account, asset, network and complete credit fingerprint; its window takes precedence over lookbackDays. A changed observation refuses the cursor, never skips or repeats a credit. Omit paging for the whole bounded observation. A window holding more than 1,000 records answers no credits with DEPOSIT_HISTORY_WINDOW_TOO_LARGE; read a shorter window. The 409 refusals of the account balance read, plus VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDING_VENUE_DISABLED when only a disabled venue holds the balance key. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED whenever the caller's read authority has ended, whether the check before the read or a recheck during it sees it (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its owner lost permission to view wallets, its membership or taker admission); a session that has itself ended answers 401.

query.description:
Initial history window, 1 to 30 days, default 7. On subsequent pages the
cursor's frozen window takes precedence; omit lookbackDays then.
Credits per page, 1 to 200. Omit for all credits; a cursor retains its page size.

The previous nextCursor. Binds the workspace, account, asset, network,
window and observed credit set. A changed observation refuses instead of skipping credits.

request.description:
Read how to deposit into the venue account

The caller must be allowed to view wallets in a company or broker workspace (or be an admitted LP taker). API keys additionally require treasury_read; this read never authorizes a payment. Read through the configured connection holding the account's balance credential. Select currency for bank instructions: bankDeposit states available, referenceOnly, notOffered or unread, with a reason and reasonCode. Available receiving coordinates or a reference-only result are in bankInstructions. notOffered comes only from the venue's declared bank offering; failed source reads are unread, never notOffered. The answer is Cache-Control no-store and every receiving-account or full-reference disclosure is audited. The connection read's selection and fee rules apply. Select payInLegId (a summary pay-in window's legId) for one open pay-in leg's payment details: the read uses that leg's currency and, for a dedicated fiat venue, the paying bank its deposit declaration recorded when that bank is linked at the venue; send it alone (400 PAY_IN_LEG_SELECTION_EXCLUSIVE). 404 PAY_IN_LEG_NOT_FOUND for a leg that is not this account's pay-in, 409 PAY_IN_LEG_NOT_OPEN once it is no longer waiting for funds, 409 PAY_IN_LEG_NOT_BANK_CURRENCY for a leg paid in a digital asset (no bank payment details; read the deposit address with asset and chainRef). VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDING_VENUE_DISABLED is answered before any payInLegId is read. The account balance read's 409 refusals also apply, plus VENUE_ACCOUNT_FUNDING_VENUE_DISABLED when only a disabled venue holds the balance key. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED whenever the caller's read authority has ended, whether the check before the read or a recheck during it sees it (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its owner lost permission to view wallets, its membership or taker admission); a session that has itself ended answers 401.

query.description: ISO fiat currency for the bank-deposit read; never with `asset` or `chainRef`.
The dedicated fiat venue's linked bank id for the sending bank. Required with currency for a dedicated fiat venue and refused for other venues.

One of the venue account's open pay-in legs (a summary pay-in window's `legId`):
the read selects that leg's currency and, for a dedicated fiat venue, the paying
bank its deposit declaration recorded. Only on the venue-account read, and never
with `asset`, `chainRef`, `currency` or `providerBankId`.

request.description:
Read the venue account's signed positions and credit line

Reads the account's ledger for a caller allowed to view the workspace's wallets. A member session reads the venue live (`source: live`). An API key or OAuth client needs treasury_read and never starts a venue read: it gets the account's last recorded observation (`source: recorded`), dated by `observedAt`, with `stale` true when it is over an hour old, or 409 LEDGER_NOT_OBSERVED when none is recorded yet, and 404 VENUE_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND for another workspace's account. Positions and credit retain separate observation and provider times. Failed credit remains unavailable while readable positions are returned. No background polling. 409 LEDGER_UNSUPPORTED means the venue does not report a ledger; LEDGER_SETUP_MISSING means its connection needs setup; VENUE_ACCOUNT_LEDGER_PENDING means the account has not finished setup, so nothing is observed yet. 403 LEDGER_ACCOUNT_FORBIDDEN without permission to view wallets on this workspace's account; foreign accounts refuse before provider I/O. 502 LEDGER_DATA_INVALID when the venue's figures cannot be read as exact amounts; 503 LEDGER_READ_UNAVAILABLE or LEDGER_JOURNAL_UNAVAILABLE when the read cannot complete, with the last good read time when one is known. A failed read is never an empty ledger.

List a venue account's settlement movements

Deposits to and withdrawals from the venue account that settle obligations, newest first, optionally for one window; page with cursor. lastSuccessfulReadAt and observationState say how current the recorded movements are. A member session also refreshes them from the LP's history; an API key or OAuth client reads the recorded movements and never starts that refresh. Required API-key scope: `settlements_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. The key's owner must also be allowed to view the workspace's settlements.

Read a settlement movement

One recorded movement with its finality and how it matched. Required API-key scope: `settlements_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. The key's owner must also be allowed to view the workspace's settlements.

List a venue account's settlement obligations

What the workspace and the LP owe each other on this account, with status and deadline, optionally for one window or one trade; page with cursor. Required API-key scope: `settlements_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. The key's owner must also be allowed to view the workspace's settlements.

Read a settlement obligation

One obligation with its status, deadline, origin and the movements matched to it. Required API-key scope: `settlements_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. The key's owner must also be allowed to view the workspace's settlements.

Read a venue account's settlement schedules

The LP's published settlement schedules for this account, the one in effect with its minimum settlement, and the next window. Required API-key scope: `settlements_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. The key's owner must also be allowed to view the workspace's settlements.

List a venue account's settlement windows

The account's settlement windows, newest snapshot first, each with its indicative statement once the snapshot is ready: positions, snapshot prices (an unavailable price names its stage and reason) and the minimum-settlement decision. Filter by state; page with cursor. Required API-key scope: `settlements_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. The key's owner must also be allowed to view the workspace's settlements.

query.description: Only windows in this snapshot state.
The previous page's `nextCursor`, unchanged.
Windows per page, 1 to 100 (default 100).

request.description:
Read a settlement window

One window with its indicative statement (positions, snapshot prices and the minimum-settlement decision), its obligations, the LP's own statement on an LP-issued window, and the movements matched to it. Required API-key scope: `settlements_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope. The key's owner must also be allowed to view the workspace's settlements.

List a settlement window's matches

The movements matched to this window's obligations, oldest first, one page at a time. Required API-key scope: `settlements_read`; an OAuth client needs the same scope.

List the workspace's venue accounts

A Company/Broker current human session, or an API key or service account with treasury_read whose owner is allowed to view wallets. Each venue account with its venue, where its funds are held, its wallets, linked accounts and execution types, each venue's key state, and whether disabling that venue would retire its key. An account-based item's `accountId` is the `{venueAccountId}` of `GET …/venue-accounts/{venueAccountId}/balances`, `/deposit-history` and `/deposit-instructions`; a walletBased item has no venue account and carries no `accountId` (its `fundingTarget` names the organisation's trading wallets). Key items by `venueEnablementId`. Oldest first, paged by `limit` (default 20, at most 100) and the opaque `cursor` from the previous page's `nextCursor`; `nextCursor` is null on the last page. A foreign or unknown path workspace answers the same 404 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND without reading that workspace. 400 INVALID_CURSOR for a cursor this list did not issue. 403 VENUE_READ_AUTHORITY_REFUSED when the caller's authority to read venue accounts has ended (reason `authority_ended`: the credential is revoked or expired, or no longer carries treasury_read; reason `permission_withdrawn`: its owner lost permission to view wallets, its membership or taker admission). A session that has itself ended answers 401.

query.description: Opaque `nextCursor` from the previous page of the same list and filters.

Page size from 1 to 100, default 20. A value outside that range is
refused with 400 `INVALID_LIMIT`, never clamped.

request.description: List webhooks

query.description: Page size, default 20, clamped to 1–100
Opaque nextCursor from this workspace's webhook list

header.description: Required for every caller (1 to 255 bytes; missing or empty is 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED). The same key and body within 24 hours answers the stored 201 again: the same webhook, with secret null and secretShownOnce true, and no second webhook is created. The same key with a different body is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

request.description:
Create a webhook

Create a webhook with a shown-once whsec_<base64> secret. Standard Webhooks sends webhook-id, webhook-timestamp (Unix seconds), and webhook-signature: v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256>, signing id.timestamp.rawBody with the base64-decoded key. Verify the exact raw body and enforce five-minute timestamp tolerance. Required API-key scope: `webhooks_manage`; the key's owner must still be allowed to manage webhooks. A member session needs permission to manage webhooks or credentials.

request.description:
Update a webhook

Update any of url, events or active without recreating the endpoint. URLs use the same HTTPS and SSRF validation as creation; events must be current subscription names. Changing url or events makes the caller the endpoint's accountable principal, whose read rights then govern protected event delivery; changing only active keeps the existing principal. Required API-key scope: `webhooks_manage`; the key's owner must still be allowed to manage webhooks. A member session needs permission to manage webhooks or credentials.

Reactivate an auto-paused webhook, resetting its failure count and pause time. Required API-key scope: `webhooks_manage`; the key's owner must still be allowed to manage webhooks. A member session needs permission to manage webhooks or credentials.

header.description: Required for every caller (1 to 255 bytes; missing or empty is 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED). The same key within 24 hours replays the stored 200 without rotating again: secret is null and secretShownOnce true. A new key rotates again. Reuse with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

request.description:
Rotate a webhook secret

Rotate a webhook's Standard Webhooks secret. Returns a shown-once whsec_<base64> secret. For 24 hours, webhook-signature carries space-separated v1,<base64> signatures from current and previous decoded keys; either verifies id.timestamp.rawBody. Required API-key scope: `webhooks_manage`; the key's owner must still be allowed to manage webhooks. A member session needs permission to manage webhooks or credentials.
